summary: Access request stuck when user identity merge causes tenant-namespace collision
description:
Issue summary: A newly onboarded contractor's access request to the internal Model Inspector console is stalled in the approval queue. The root trigger appears to be an identity merge event where two Okta profiles were consolidated and the tenant namespace value collided with an existing service-account namespace.

Impact: A single contractor (and possibly others with similar legacy accounts) cannot complete just-in-time provisioning; UI shows 'Provisioning queued' indefinitely and no service token is issued. This blocks onboarding tasks and time-sensitive runbook work.

Context: Customer-facing systems are unaffected; this ticket is for internal onboarding and RBAC provisioning flows. We suspect this is an edge case in the SCIM merge pipeline that incorrectly marks an identity as 'reserved' and prevents runbook provisioning from selecting a new namespace.
impact: One contractor cannot get console access; potential for additional stalled onboarding requests if identity merges occur for older external_id formats.
steps_to_reproduce: Create two Okta test accounts: one legacy with external_id format 'org:user:123' and a new federated account 'okta|user@example.com'.
Trigger a SCIM identity merge that consolidates the legacy external_id into the federated profile (simulate via scim-merge tool in staging where possible).
Submit an access request for the merged identity to access the Model Inspector console via the support portal.
Observe approval queue status and whether the provisioning runbook issues a service token or stalls with a 'namespace reserved' state.
observed_behavior: Access request status remains 'Provisioning queued' for >24 hours. Audit logs show 'namespace conflict: tenant_x already reserved by service-account' while the identity's external_id was updated. No token was minted and runbook never executed. SCIM merge log shows the legacy external_id was appended as an alias rather than removed.
expected_behavior: After identity merge, provisioning should either select an available namespace or surface a clear actionable error that routes to identity-team. The access request should progress to 'Provisioned' with a service token minted, or fail with actionable remediation.
logs: 2026-03-13T09:22:11Z - scim-merge: merged external_id org:user:123 -> okta|user@example.com, aliases=[org:user:123], outcome=aliases_preserved
2026-03-13T09:22:12Z - provisioning-runner: queued job id=pr-78945 tenant_check: reserved=true reason='namespace already bound to svc-account:svc-runner-42'
2026-03-13T09:22:12Z - provisioning-runner: aborting job id=pr-78945, error='tenant namespace collision', attempt=1
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: SCIM merge preserves legacy external_id as a live alias that provisioning treats as primary tenant namespace, causing collision with existing service accounts created before aliasing rules changed.
Hypothesis 2: Provisioning logic uses the first seen namespace string across identities without deduplicating aliases; merge order can flip which namespace is considered canonical.
Checked related audit traces: identity-service shows merge event and alias-preserve flag. Linked runbook execution never progressed past tenant_check.
comments: 2026-03-13 10:05 - Miguel Ramirez (assignee): Assigned and reproducing locally in a disposable tenant. Initial repro in staging succeeded in creating a collision when alias preservation is enabled.

2026-03-13 15:40 - Priya Shah (Identity): Noted that a recent SCIM change (PR #1824) toggled default alias behavior for legacy external_id formats. Opening a quick revert in staging to confirm. See GH PR: github.com/redwood-internal/scim/PR/1824.

2026-03-14 08:12 - SRE Oncall: Observed a single other onboarding case at 2026-03-12 23:11 with the same error pattern. Adding a temporary alert rule to catch 'tenant namespace collision' errors for provisioning-runner in prod/us-east.
next_steps: 1) Identity team to patch SCIM merge to remove legacy external_id from canonical namespace list when alias_preserve=true (rollback PR 1824 in staging for verification).
2) Provisioning team to add dedupe pass on namespace selection and surface non-blocking error in the access-request UI to route to identity-team if collision detected.
3) SRE to deploy a temporary alert for 'tenant namespace collision' and run a query for similar events in the last 30 days to scope impact.
4) Once patch validated in staging, schedule a staged rollout to prod with a canary for 10% of onboarding flows, monitor alert and access-request latency.
